stem: Each option describes a faxed Schedule II prescription. In which cases may the fax serve as the original under a specific federal exception, assuming all other requirements are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Methylphenidate for a resident of a long-term-care facility
Oxycodone for a hospice patient when the prescription indicates hospice status
Fentanyl to be compounded for direct continuous intravenous infusion
Dexmethylphenidate for a hospice patient, relying only on hospice status
Oxycodone tablets for a routine ambulatory patient with no LTCF, hospice, or qualifying infusion facts

explanation.core_reasoning: Schedule II status alone is insufficient; LTCF status, hospice+narcotic status, or a qualifying compounded narcotic route triggers the fax-as-original exceptions.

choice_analysis.A: The LTCF exception applies to a C-II prescription without a narcotic-only limit.
choice_analysis.B: A C-II narcotic hospice prescription can qualify.
choice_analysis.C: A qualifying C-II narcotic compounded infusion can qualify.
choice_analysis.D: The hospice exception is for a C-II narcotic; this stimulant is nonnarcotic.
choice_analysis.E: The ordinary fax is not itself the original.

related_facts: The LTCF exception is not limited to narcotics.
explanation.mpje_trap: Using one exception's narcotic requirement for all faxed C-II prescriptions.

reasoning_steps: Recognize that every option is Schedule II
Classify setting, narcotic status, and formulation
